text.p: Anti-federalists in the European Parliament, including Anglo-French billionaire Sir James Goldsmith, found themselves stranded on Monday when their Europe of Nations (EDN) party was officially dissolved.
The demise was provoked by the defection to the conservative Union for Europe group by French Euro-MP Anne Christine Poisson, which cut the EDN's numbers to 17.
The EDN needed a minimum of 18 members to survive.

Paavo Vayryaen, one of Finland's newly elected deputies and the translator of a Goldsmith book attacking global free trade, was expected to make up for Poisson's departure by taking a seat with the EDN when he officially entered the EU assembly on Monday.
But Vayrynaen followed his four collegues from Finland's Centre Party and aligned himself with the Liberals in the EU's directly-elected Parliament.

Parliament officials say privately it appears Vayrynaen came under pressure from British conservative Euro-MPs into not siding with Sir James, whose Referendum Party in Britain claims growing support from traditional Conservative voters fearful of European federalism and the influence of Brussels.
The EDN has formally denied rumours it asked Austrian nationalist Joerg Haider, who heads Europe's biggest far-right grouping, to bring his Freedom Party (FPO) into their fold.
The FPO scored its biggest electoral success to date in a European parliamentary poll in October.
Its six Euro-MPs say they wil work with other like-minded groups in the Strasbourg-based Parliament to push for a review of the Maastricht Treaty.
Goldsmith, who amassed a fortune as an entrepeneur, wants a referendum on Britain's future in Europe and says he will dissolve his party once this objective is achieved.
He plans to put forward about 600 candidates at the British general election next year.
